function far_spruce(b, x, base, h, w, p)
  b:load(p, 0.75)
  local lean = rand(-0.04, 0.04)
  b:stroke({{x + lean*h, base - h}, {x, base}}, {pressure={0.05, 0.7}})
  local y = base - h + 1.5
  local i = 0
  while y < base do

    local sag = half * rand(0.15, 0.4)
    if rand(0,1) < 0.85 then b:stroke({{xx - half, y + sag}, {xx - half*0.4, y + sag*0.3}, {xx, y - 0.5}}, {pressure={0.15, 0.35}}) end

    y = y + rand(1.2, 3.0) * (0.7 + 0.6*t)

function big_spruce(cx, top, base, halfw, pile_, seed, opts)
  opts = opts or {}
  math.randomseed(seed)
  local lean = opts.lean or 0
  local fw = opts.fw or 16
  local f = brush{kind="fan", width=fw, lay=2.5}
  local fs = brush{kind="fan", width=fw*0.55, lay=2}
  local wob = noise{seed=seed, period=90, octaves=2}
  local env = noise{seed=seed + 7, period=opts.envp or 70, octaves=2}
  local function xc(y) return cx + lean * (base - y) + 2.5*wob(cx, y) end
  local tw = opts.trunk or 6
  local lead = brush{kind="round", width=tw, point=0.7}
  lead:load(pile_, 1.0)
  lead:gesture({{xc(top), top, 0.03}, {xc(top + (base-top)*0.25), top + (base-top)*0.25, 0.35}, {xc(base - (base-top)*0.3), base - (base-top)*0.3, 0.8}, {xc(base), base, 1.0}})
  f:load(pile_, 1.0); fs:load(pile_, 1.0)
  local y = top + 3
  local n = 0
  while y < base - (opts.skirt or 0) do
    local t = (y - top) / (base - top)
    local half = halfw * (0.04 + 0.96 * t^0.85) * (0.82 + 0.4 * env(0, y))
    local b = (t < 0.12) and fs or f
    local skip = (t > 0.3 and rand(0,1) < (opts.skip or 0.08))
    if not skip then
      for side = -1, 1, 2 do
        if rand(0,1) > (opts.gap or 0.1) then
          local L = half * rand(0.65, 1.05)
          if rand(0,1) < 0.1 then L = L * rand(1.15, 1.35) end
          local x0 = xc(y)
          local droop = L * (0.12 + 0.35 * t) * rand(0.7, 1.3)
          local lift = L * rand(-0.05, 0.14)
          b:stroke({{x0, y}, {x0 + side*L*0.45, y + droop*0.65}, {x0 + side*L*0.85, y + droop}, {x0 + side*L, y + droop - lift}}, {pressure={rand(0.6, 0.9), 0.05}, orient="across", ramps={0.05, 0.6}})
          n = n + 1
          if t > 0.15 and rand(0,1) < 0.75 then
            local L2 = L * rand(0.35, 0.7)
            local yy = y + rand(3, 7) * (0.5 + t)
            b:stroke({{x0, yy}, {x0 + side*L2*0.6, yy + droop*0.6}, {x0 + side*L2, yy + droop*0.9}}, {pressure={0.75, 0.1}, orient="across"})
            n = n + 1
          end
          if n % 3 == 0 then f:load(pile_, 0.85); fs:load(pile_, 0.8) end
        end
      end
    end
    y = y + (2.5 + 11 * t) * rand(0.6, 1.4)
  end
  return n
end

    n = n + 1

end

lw = pile{{"lead white", 1}, medium=0.45, name="liquid_white"}
sky_mid = pile{{"lead white", 4}, {"cobalt blue", 0.45}, {"vermilion", 0.22}, name="sky_mid"}
work(everywhere(), {hand="broad", pile=lw, coverage=1.5, load=0.5, angle=0})

blend(everywhere(), {angle=0})
tree_dark = pile{{"Prussian blue", 0.6}, {"raw umber", 1}, {"bone black", 0.5}, name="tree_dark"}
function big_spruce(cx, top, base, halfw, pile_, seed, opts)
  opts = opts or {}
  math.randomseed(seed)
  local lean = opts.lean or 0
  local fw = opts.fw or 16
  local f = brush{kind="fan", width=fw, lay=2.5}
  local fs = brush{kind="fan", width=fw*0.55, lay=2}
  local wob = noise{seed=seed, period=90, octaves=2}
  local env = noise{seed=seed + 7, period=opts.envp or 70, octaves=2}
  local function xc(y) return cx + lean * (base - y) + 2.5*wob(cx, y) end
  local tw = opts.trunk or 6
  local lead = brush{kind="round", width=tw, point=0.7}
  lead:load(pile_, 1.0)
  lead:gesture({{xc(top), top, 0.03}, {xc(top + (base-top)*0.25), top + (base-top)*0.25, 0.35}, {xc(base - (base-top)*0.3), base - (base-top)*0.3, 0.8}, {xc(base), base, 1.0}})
  f:load(pile_, 1.0); fs:load(pile_, 1.0)
  local y = top + 3
  local n = 0
  local br = {}
  while y < base - (opts.skirt or 0) do
    local t = (y - top) / (base - top)
    local half = halfw * (0.04 + 0.96 * t^0.85) * (0.82 + 0.4 * env(0, y))
    local b = (t < 0.12) and fs or f
    local skip = (t > 0.3 and rand(0,1) < (opts.skip or 0.08))
    if not skip then
      for side = -1, 1, 2 do
        if rand(0,1) > (opts.gap or 0.1) then
          local L = half * rand(0.65, 1.05)
          if rand(0,1) < 0.1 then L = L * rand(1.15, 1.35) end
          local x0 = xc(y)
          local droop = L * (0.12 + 0.35 * t) * rand(0.7, 1.3)
          local lift = L * rand(-0.05, 0.14)
          b:stroke({{x0, y}, {x0 + side*L*0.45, y + droop*0.65}, {x0 + side*L*0.85, y + droop}, {x0 + side*L, y + droop - lift}}, {pressure={rand(0.6, 0.9), 0.05}, orient="across", ramps={0.05, 0.6}})
          br[#br+1] = {x0, y, side, L, droop, lift}
          n = n + 1
          if t > 0.15 and rand(0,1) < 0.75 then
            local L2 = L * rand(0.35, 0.7)
            local yy = y + rand(3, 7) * (0.5 + t)
            b:stroke({{x0, yy}, {x0 + side*L2*0.6, yy + droop*0.6}, {x0 + side*L2, yy + droop*0.9}}, {pressure={0.75, 0.1}, orient="across"})
            n = n + 1
          end
          if n % 3 == 0 then f:load(pile_, 0.85); fs:load(pile_, 0.8) end
        end
      end
    end
    y = y + (2.5 + 11 * t) * rand(0.6, 1.4)
  end
  return br
end

-- sparse branch pass that remembers where its branches are
function spruce_branches(cx, top, base, halfw, pile_, seed, opts)
  opts = opts or {}
  math.randomseed(seed)
  local fw = opts.fw or 16
  local f = brush{kind="fan", width=fw, lay=2.5}
  local fs = brush{kind="fan", width=fw*0.55, lay=2}
  local wob = noise{seed=seed, period=90, octaves=2}
  local env = noise{seed=seed + 7, period=70, octaves=2}
  local function xc(y) return cx + 2.5*wob(cx, y) end
  f:load(pile_, 1.0); fs:load(pile_, 1.0)
  local y = top + 3
  local n = 0
  local br = {}
  while y < base - (opts.skirt or 0) do
    local t = (y - top) / (base - top)
    local half = halfw * (0.04 + 0.96 * t^0.85) * (0.82 + 0.4 * env(0, y))
    local b = (t < 0.12) and fs or f
    for side = -1, 1, 2 do
      if rand(0,1) > (opts.gap or 0.55) then
        local L = half * rand(0.6, 1.0)
        local x0 = xc(y)
        local droop = L * (0.12 + 0.35 * t) * rand(0.7, 1.3)
        local lift = L * rand(-0.05, 0.14)
        b:stroke({{x0, y}, {x0 + side*L*0.45, y + droop*0.65}, {x0 + side*L*0.85, y + droop}, {x0 + side*L, y + droop - lift}}, {pressure={rand(0.6, 0.9), 0.05}, orient="across", ramps={0.05, 0.6}})
        br[#br+1] = {x0, y, side, L, droop, lift, t}
        n = n + 1
        if n % 3 == 0 then f:load(pile_, 0.85); fs:load(pile_, 0.8) end
      end
    end
    y = y + (3 + 13 * t) * rand(0.6, 1.4)
  end
  return br
end
function tree_highlights2(br, p, opts)
  opts = opts or {}
  local f = brush{kind="fan", width=opts.fw or 7, lay=1.4}
  local n = 0
  for i, b in ipairs(br) do

    local want = (side == -1) and (opts.left or 0.7) or (opts.right or 0.1)
    if opts.tmax and t > opts.tmax then want = 0 end
    if opts.tmin and t < opts.tmin then want = 0 end
    if rand(0,1) < want then

      for j = 1, k do

        local u1 = math.min(0.95, u0 + rand(0.15, 0.3))

        local xb, yb = x0 + side*L*u1, y + droop*u1*0.9 - lift*u1 - 1.5
        f:stroke({{xa, ya}, {xb, yb}}, {pressure={opts.p0 or 0.32, 0.08}, orient="across"})

function tree_lights(br, p, opts)
  opts = opts or {}
  local f = brush{kind="fan", width=opts.fw or 8, lay=1.5}
  local n = 0
  for i, b in ipairs(br) do
    local x0, y, side, L, droop, lift, t = table.unpack(b)
    t = t or 0.5
    local want = (side == -1) and (opts.left or 0.6) or (opts.right or 0.2)
    if opts.tmax and t > opts.tmax then want = want * 0.3 end
    if rand(0,1) < want then
      if n % 2 == 0 then f:wipe(0.7); f:load(p, opts.load or 0.45) end
      local function pt(u) return {x0 + side*L*u, y + droop*u*0.85 - lift*u*u - 1.5} end
      local u0 = rand(0.25, 0.5)
      f:stroke({pt(u0), pt((u0 + 0.95)/2), pt(0.95)}, {pressure={opts.p0 or 0.4, 0.08}, orient="across", ramps={0.15, 0.5}})
      n = n + 1
    end
  end
  return n
end

function break_branches(br, p, fw, seed)
  math.randomseed(seed)
  local f = brush{kind="fan", width=fw, lay=2.0}

    f:stroke({pt(u0), pt((u0+u1)/2), pt(u1)}, {pressure={rand(0.45, 0.7), 0.1}, orient="across", ramps={0.1, 0.5}})

function spruce_patch(cx, top, base, halfw, y0, y1, pile_, seed, fw, sides)
  math.randomseed(seed)
  local f = brush{kind="fan", width=fw, lay=2.5}
  f:load(pile_, 1.0)
  local y = y0
  local n = 0
  while y < y1 do
    local t = (y - top) / (base - top)
    local half = halfw * (0.04 + 0.96 * t^0.85) * rand(0.8, 1.1)
    for _, side in ipairs(sides or {-1, 1}) do
      local L = half * rand(0.7, 1.05)
      local droop = L * (0.12 + 0.35 * t) * rand(0.7, 1.3)
      local lift = L * rand(-0.05, 0.14)
      f:stroke({{cx, y}, {cx + side*L*0.45, y + droop*0.65}, {cx + side*L*0.85, y + droop}, {cx + side*L, y + droop - lift}}, {pressure={rand(0.6, 0.9), 0.05}, orient="across", ramps={0.05, 0.6}})
      n = n + 1
      if n % 3 == 0 then f:load(pile_, 0.85) end
    end
    y = y + (2.5 + 11 * t) * rand(0.6, 1.2)
  end
  return n
end

function wind_line(br, p, x0, y0, len, seed)
  math.randomseed(seed)
  local x = x0
  local xe = x0 + len
  while x < xe do
    local seg = rand(12, 45)
    local x1 = math.min(xe, x + seg)
    local yy = y0 + rand(-0.6, 0.6)
    br:reload(p, rand(0.3, 0.5))
    local xm = (x + x1) / 2
    br:stroke({{x, yy + rand(-0.3, 0.3)}, {xm, yy + rand(-0.5, 0.5)}, {x1, yy + rand(-0.3, 0.3)}}, {pressure={rand(0.1, 0.2), 0.03}, ramps={0.35, 0.5}})
    x = x1 + rand(2, 14)
  end
end

ripple_w = mix{{sky_mid, 0.6}, {sky_low, 0.25}, {water_deep, 0.15}, name="ripple_w"}
function wind_line(br, p, x0, y0, len, seed, pr)
  math.randomseed(seed)
  local x = x0
  local xe = x0 + len
  while x < xe do
    local seg = rand(12, 45)
    local x1 = math.min(xe, x + seg)
    local yy = y0 + rand(-0.6, 0.6)
    br:reload(p, rand(0.3, 0.5))
    local xm = (x + x1) / 2
    br:stroke({{x, yy + rand(-0.3, 0.3)}, {xm, yy + rand(-0.5, 0.5)}, {x1, yy + rand(-0.3, 0.3)}}, {pressure={rand(pr[1], pr[2]), 0.03}, ramps={0.35, 0.5}})
    x = x1 + rand(2, 14)
  end
end

## Day 1, 18:42-22:50 campaigns
- Water lines: knife (width 40, blade angle 0.1-0.26, p 0.6, load 0.25) of sky_mid/sky_low = bright crisp bars, far too strong; the knife also crossed the right-hand spruces and laid pale stripes through them. Blending them along ribbons only widened them into soft bars. Repair that worked: repaint each bar's ribbon (16 wide, soften 3) with short vertical filbert-6 strokes (cov 1.0, load 0.4) from piles weighted by which zone the point is in (refl_mtn / caps / glow / blue), then a light horizontal blend. Stripes through the trees: re-stroked with tree_dark (round 5, point 0, lay 2, reload 1.0, two strokes per side per tree) - covered.
- Lesson: a crisp knife line of a light pile reads as a white bar at this scale; for water lines use rigger 'wind_line' segments (rigger 2.5, reload 0.3-0.5, p 0.1-0.2, gaps 2-14) of a mix only a step lighter than the water (ripple_c = sky_mid .7 + refl_dark .3): subtle broken lines. On the pale glow water the same lines are invisible (accepted).
- Reflection rework: the earlier wipe + repaint had left the mountain reflection's lower part pale and the snowcap reflection a misshapen blob. Wiped the cap zone with a spirits rag, repainted in 4 zones (dark above an inverted ragged snowline, sky outside the ridges, lit/shade snow either side of the inverted rib), dark rib strokes, vertical blends. Then strengthened the bright lit edge of the inverted west ridge (cap_bright). Now reads as the peak's mirror image.
- Pale far-shore halo: the water strip just below the far shore was much lighter (190) than the water below (157). Repainted ribbon strips with water_F / water_L mixes matched by scratch probes (target ~158), then a broad clipped pass (cov 1, load .3, p .2-.4) over y 489-540 minus trees_mask, blended; an edge blend vertical at 524-556. Halo gone.
- A rectangular repaint patch (x 668-742, y 624-706) behind the small trees left a visible box; fixed by covering with refl_dark at soften(10) + blend, then softening its edges with a horizontal blend and repainting the small trees and boughs over it. Lesson: patch masks need soft edges >= 10 and must follow natural boundaries; a hard rect repaint shows as a box against the gradient.
- Alpenglow: knife (20) of alpenglow pile (white 5, vermilion .42, chrome .3, blot .15) on the upper west ridge, p .3-.55: subtle warm pink on the summit.
- Grass tufts: tuft() 3-7 curved rigger blades from a root, land_dark/grass_dusk, plus a darker lower bank (body land_dark cov 1.5): the bank now has weight and the lit rim reads as backlit grass.
- Signature: small 'C' and underline at lower right (rigger 1.5, sig pile red earth/ochre/white, medium .15).

The painting held up fine over the week since the thick paint with raw umber and Prussian blue in the dark trees stayed open longer than usual. Since the brief calls for wet-on-wet technique, I did everything in one sitting on day one, so waiting a week afterward was just about letting it dry rather than continuing to work into it.

Reviewing areas now: the snow line on the mountain's lit face is slightly too uniform but reads acceptably, the scattered snow patches on the lower face are a touch regularly spaced but passable, the pale water glow area is flat but the ripple dashes work, and the outer tree boughs have some flat plane marks that are fine. Since the paint is now dry, any additional work would mean glazing over dry paint rather than true wet-on-wet.

So the real question becomes procedural: the piece is considered finished only when a sitting passes with no new marks made, following a review of the whole and a detail crop. Since this sitting has involved active marks, I'm thinking through whether I can treat this as the close of one sitting and open a new one within the same conversation just to look — though that feels like it might be gaming the rule rather than honoring it. The cleanest path is to write a handoff now noting any open passages, and let the painting's completion be confirmed in a genuinely separate, mark-free sitting rather than declaring it done myself.

Before writing that handoff though, I want to scrutinize the piece one more time for weak points — specifically the large pale glow reflection in the lower-left water, which is quite dominant (roughly a sixth of the canvas) and whose diagonal edge mirrors the left ridge rather strongly. I'm checking whether that reflection's geometry actually lines up with where the mountain's slope would project onto the water, since it looks slightly off from where the ridge descends.

Checking the numbers, the reflection position is close enough to be consistent with the skyline height above the waterline. The mist band reflection, the heavy dark tree silhouettes on the right (intentional for the dusk contrejour effect), the brown land and signature in the corner, and the tiny spit trees on the left all look fine — the one soft spot might be that the main lit snowfield feels a touch flat, though that's acceptable.

I'm weighing whether to push for more refinement, but each additional repair risks undoing a coherent effect, so I'm leaning toward stopping and noting there are no real open passages — just checking a couple of tiny details first, like the faint dashed ripple lines in the reflection (which read fine as wind lines) and a small pale fleck near the reflection that might just be an inverted summit rib.

That stray tick appears to sit within the dark mountain reflection — plausible as a snow patch echo, so I'll let it be. Since the paint has mostly dried except for the thick tree impasto, any further intervention would mean reworking over dry paint, which goes against the wet-on-wet alla prima approach, so I'm ready to finalize the handoff noting no open passages remain, in keeping with the brief's definition of a finished sitting.

The tree at x=900 and the thick dark layer remain open, though that's not critical. Let me grab one more detail crop of the left bank and water at full resolution in normal color before writing the journal entry.

## Handoff, end of sitting 1 (day 8, 22:50 after a 7-day wait)
The whole picture was laid wet-on-wet on day 1 (09:00-22:50 painting time) over liquid white, then left to dry for a week. Almost all of it is touch-dry now; the thick fan-brush spruce darks at the right (lay 2.5) are still open. Any further work would go over dry paint and break the alla prima unity, so I'm leaving the surface alone unless a later look finds a real fault.

State: glow low-left, cobalt sky with thin lit cirrus; snow peak right of center, knife-laid snow with warm alpenglow on its west faces and cool east faces; mist at its foot; far shore of small spruces; still lake holding the glow, the peak's mirror image and faint wind lines; dark spruce stand at right, grassy bank with three boulders at lower left. Signature 'C' lower right.

Accepted on purpose (not open): the snow flecks on the lower mountain are scattered fairly evenly (they read as late-season patches at viewing distance); the wind lines on the dark reflection are faint dashes; the big glow reflection at lower left is plain and flat (it's the quiet passage that carries the light into the picture).

Open passages: none

Lessons to carry forward (observed at this easel, conditions as stated; general rules are hypotheses):
- Liquid white (lead white + medium 0.45, broad, cov 1.5, load 0.5) stays open all day and lightens everything laid into it. Plan pile values a step darker than the target.
- Never blend across a large rectangle of mixed values: the badger lifts thin paint and leaves boxes (observed twice). Blend only shaped masks that follow the passage's natural edges, soften >= 6-10, and subtract what must stay crisp (trees_mask, refl_mtn, caps).
- Repairs with a spirits rag (dip 0.9, p 0.75-0.8, 2 passes + a cross pass, refold 0.35-0.45) take open paint down to an even pale tint; repaint with piles matched by scratch probes (lay a 200x150 patch of each candidate mix over liquid white and probe it, aiming within ~5 of the neighbour's value).
- Knife snow over wet dark: blotted white (blot 0.15), knife 22-34, load 0.35-0.5, pressure 0.15-0.25 rising to 0.3-0.55, blade ~1 rad off the path: opaque slabs that keep their edges. Above p 0.5 the knife only leaves fine broken lines.
- A knife line of light paint across water reads as a hard white bar at this scale. Use broken rigger segments a single value step lighter than the water.
- Light marks on wet dark spruce (fan, blotted light green) read as rows of dots. Better: cool blue-gray planes (tree_mid2) along the outer boughs, then re-stroking random partial branches in the dark (break_branches) to break up the regularity.
- Fan spruce: strokes from the trunk outward, pressure 0.6-0.9 falling to 0.05, orient across, droop growing toward the base, second shorter stroke below. Store branch geometry so later passes can follow it.
- The palette holds 16 piles; scrape mixes as soon as a passage is done.
Uncertain: how much the thick open tree paint will move if touched later. It's still open after 7 days, so check drying() before any work there.

content.text:
**Last Light on the Tarn**

A small mountain lake just after sunset, in late autumn after the first snow. The glow is low on the left, where the sun has gone down. The snow peak right of centre still catches a little warm pink on its west faces, and its east faces have gone cool blue-violet. At its foot, mist lies over a far shore of small spruces. The still water carries three things: the pale gold of the glow, the peak's mirror image and a few faint wind lines. A dark stand of spruce rises on the right, and a grassy bank with three boulders closes the lower left.

I painted it all wet-on-wet in one day of painting time, over a thin wet coat of white thinned with oil. The sky went on in crossing strokes and was blended out. The snow was laid with the knife into the wet dark of the mountain, and the reflections were pulled down and softened with a blender. The fan-brush trees and the grass came last. Then I let it dry for a week. Almost all of it is touch-dry now; the thickest paint in the right-hand spruces is still wet.

Several passages needed repairs along the way:
- **Water:** blending across the whole lake lifted the paint into pale boxes, and I wiped it back with a rag dipped in solvent and repainted it.
- **Lake surface:** knife-laid light lines came out as hard white bars across the water and the trees. I painted over them and replaced them with fainter broken lines.
- **Spruces:** light dabs on the dark trees read as rows of dots. I painted them back out, then broke up the boughs with cooler grey-blue planes and dark restrokes.

Some things I've left as they are on purpose: the even scatter of snow patches on the lower mountain, the faint dashes on the dark reflection, and the plain, flat glow reflection at the lower left. The journal lists no open passages, so a next sitting only needs to look at the picture and confirm it. The journal also records the recipes and lessons from this sitting.
